record.original_question: Plessner [636] proves after Privaloff that if f is analytic in D, almost all points P of the boundary are of two kinds. Either (a) f tends to a finite limit, as z → P in any Stolz angle S, lying in D, or (b) as z → P in any S, f takes (infinitely) often all values of a dense set. Can ‘dense set’ be replaced by anything bigger here; e.g. the complement of a set of measure zero? (E. F. Collingwood)

evidence.quote: Plessner [636] proves after Privaloff that if f is analytic in D, almost all points P of the boundary are of two kinds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a holomorphic function. For a boundary point $P\in\partial\mathbb{D}$, a Stolz angle at $P$ is the interior of the convex hull of $\{P\}$ together with a closed disc $\overline{D(0,r)}$ for some $r\in(0,1)$ (equivalently, a non-tangential approach region with vertex at $P$ contained in $\mathbb{D}$).

Plessner's theorem (after Privaloff) asserts that for almost every (with respect to Lebesgue arclength measure) boundary point $P\in\partial\mathbb{D}$, exactly one of the following holds:
(a) $f(z)$ tends to a finite limit as $z\to P$ within every Stolz angle $S$ at $P$ (i.e. $P$ is a Fatou point); or
(b) for every Stolz angle $S$ at $P$, the function $f$ takes (infinitely often) every value of some set $E_{P,S}\subset\mathbb{C}$ that is dense in $\mathbb{C}$.

Question. Can the conclusion in (b) be strengthened by replacing the requirement that $E_{P,S}$ be dense in $\mathbb{C}$ with the requirement that $\mathbb{C}\setminus E_{P,S}$ have planar Lebesgue measure zero (or some other property strictly stronger than density), so that the strengthened statement still holds for almost every $P\in\partial\mathbb{D}$ and every holomorphic $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work of Gardiner and Manolaki ("A strong form of Plessner's theorem", arXiv:2011.05874, published in Advances in Mathematics) shows that the density assertion in Plessner's theorem can be replaced by a substantially stronger conclusion (a universality-type statement strengthening classical results of Spencer, Stein and Carleson). Earlier improvements by Bagemihl–Piranian and others also exist. These works affirmatively strengthen the conclusion beyond mere density, so Collingwood's question is at least partially resolved, although the exact formulation in terms of "complement of a set of measure zero" varies between strengthenings.

status_evidence.title: A strong form of Plessner's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: We show that statement (ii) [the density assertion in Plessner's theorem] can be replaced by a much stronger assertion. This new theorem... also strengthens classical results of Spencer, Stein and Carleson.
status_evidence.claim: Plessner's density conclusion has been strengthened, partially answering Collingwood's question.

status_evidence.title: Plessner theorem - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: For almost every boundary point either f has a finite nontangential limit, or the image of any Stolz angle is dense in the complex plane.
status_evidence.claim: Standard form of Plessner's theorem with the density conclusion.

status_evidence.title: An improvement on Plessner's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements on Plessner's theorem regarding boundary cluster sets.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple improvements of Plessner's theorem exist in the literature.
